# Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments
Feature: wfx-erp-product-fa · Owner: Varun Kumar (VP - Technology)
Functional specification for the development team, generated from the product-team-approved Product Mock Studio screens (feature library wfx-erp-product-fa). The mock is intentionally lenient; this specification is not — it is the contract the development team builds from before it goes to QA and live production. Because the product team was not available for the pre-finalization question batch, this document ADOPTS the proposed defaults as ASSUMED (marked where used); each is listed in Section 8 for sign-off.

## Overview

### Purpose
Accounts Payable (AP) takes a supplier-side document from “validated” through to “paid”. This feature covers that pipeline across just two screens. A single status-aware screen, AP Posting & Payments, lets the AP clerk post validated documents to the ledger, schedule their expected payment dates, and gather dated documents into payment batches — without leaving the screen. A second screen, Payment Batches, is the register where a Draft batch is released (Confirm Payment) or cancelled. Four payable document types flow through: Supplier Invoice, Credit Note (a negative payable), Expense Invoice, and Advance.

### Who uses it
• AP clerks / accountants — post validated documents, assign expected payment dates, and assemble payment batches (all on one screen).
• AP / finance managers — confirm (release) or cancel payment batches.
• Downstream / reporting — read the resulting ledger entries and payment status; they do not act on these screens.

### Where it sits in the ERP?
The feature lives in the Finance & Accounting module (real target: libs/angular/features/wfx-erp/wfx-erp-fa). In the Product Mock Studio it is mounted at /accounts-payable under the app base href /wfx-erp-product/, menu label “Accounts Payable” (icon pi pi-wallet). It is downstream of purchasing/GRN (which produce the documents) and upstream of the cash/bank and general-ledger modules (which the postings and payments feed).
Scope of this spec: the two AP screens (AP Posting & Payments, Payment Batches) and the shared AP document detail right-panel. Document capture/validation (Draft → Validated) and the GL posting engine itself are upstream/downstream and out of scope (Section 7).

## Screen inventory & navigation flow

[TABLE 1: Table 1 · 3 rows · columns: # (text), Screen (text), Route (text), Purpose (text)]
| # | Screen | Route | Purpose |
| S-1 | AP Posting & Payments | /accounts-payable/posting | Status-aware working list of Validated and Posted documents. Post / UnValidate (Validated); assign Expected Payment Date and build a Payment Batch (Posted). Entry point — /accounts-payable redirects here. |
| S-2 | Payment Batches | /accounts-payable/batches | Register of every payment batch; Confirm Payment or Cancel a Draft batch. |
| S-3 | AP document detail panel | (right drawer on S-1) | Shared read-only side panel: document header + the balanced debit/credit journal preview. |
Merge history: an earlier draft had four screens (AP Posting, Expected Payment Date, Payment Batch, Payment Batches). Posting, expected-payment-date scheduling and payment-batch creation are now one status-aware screen (S-1); Payment Batches (S-2) remains the release register.

### Navigation rules
• The two screens are sibling menu links under Accounts Payable. There is no forced wizard — the clerk works the stage they need via the Status filter on S-1.
• List → detail panel: on S-1, clicking the Doc No link (data-action="open-doc") opens the shared right drawer (S-3). On S-2, clicking the Batch No link (data-action="open-batch") opens the batch detail drawer.
• Drawers are dismissible (X / overlay / hide); they never navigate away from the list.
• Documents move between stages by status, not by routing: after any action the list reloads and the acted-on rows drop off if they no longer qualify for the current Status filter.
• Browser/page titles come from the route title: “AP Posting & Payments”, “Payment Batches”.
Back-navigation / list-state retention (search, filters, sort, page, the From/To range) is not preserved by the mock across drawer opens or re-entry. The real screens must restore list state on return (QA checklist §5) — see Q-11.

## Conventions
Rules referenced throughout the field tables and the Validations master list are defined once here, so no rule restates them.

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 3 rows · columns: Convention (text), Definition (text)]
| Convention | Definition |
| Enforcement | Selection-driven toolbar and list rules are applied in the AP Posting & Payments list UI and re-checked on the server before the action commits. |
| Amounts | Displayed as the currency symbol + 2 decimals + ISO code. |
| Date display | All dates display via the app-wide WfxDateFormatService (user preference, default dd MMM yyyy) — never a hardcoded locale. |

## Screen specifications

### AP Posting & Payments (S-1)
Purpose: one status-aware list covering the AP pipeline up to payment. A Status filter chooses the stage; the toolbar actions follow the current selection, so the clerk posts, schedules, and batches from a single screen.
AP Posting & Payments — default “To Post” (Validated) view, Team Data
Posted view: Status = Posted, the Expected Pay From/To range filter, the Expected Pay Date column, and — with two dated rows selected — the Expected Pay Date and Payment Batch actions

#### Layout
• Page header: breadcrumb “Accounts Payable”, title “AP Posting & Payments”, subtitle, and the selection-driven action buttons (top right).
• Content toolbar: quick-search input (“Search by doc no. or supplier”), a Status filter, the Expected Pay From/To range filter (Posted view only), and a Doc Type dropdown.
• Grid inside a surface card; floating filter row; pagination footer (page sizes 20/50/100, default 20).

#### Status filter & views
• The Status filter has two options — To Post (Validated) and Posted — and defaults to Validated. Clearing it shows both stages at once.
• The Expected Pay Date column shows whenever Posted documents can appear (Posted view or the cleared “both” view); it is hidden in the Validated-only view.
• Switching the Status filter clears the current selection so the action buttons stay honest. Only Validated and Posted documents ever appear on this screen (Draft/In Batch/Paid do not).
• The list is ordered with dated documents first (ascending by expected date, which helps batching), then undated documents.

#### Toolbar actions (selection-driven)
The action buttons shown depend on the status of the selected rows (V-1):

[TABLE 3: Table 3 · 4 rows · columns: Selection (text), Buttons shown (text), Action (text) · identifiers: Selection]
| Selection | Buttons shown | Action |
| All Validated | UnValidate · Post | UnValidate → Draft; Post → Posted (3.1.6). |
| All Posted | Expected Pay Date | Assign / revise the expected payment date (3.1.7). |
| All Posted, every row already dated | Expected Pay Date · Payment Batch | Additionally build a payment batch (3.1.8). |
| Mixed / empty | (none) | No bulk action; narrow by Status first. |

#### Grid specification

[TABLE 4: Table 4 · 11 rows · columns: Column (text), Content & combined cells (text), Filter (text), Format / behaviour (text) · identifiers: Column]
| Column | Content & combined cells | Filter | Format / behaviour |
| (selection) | Row checkbox + header checkbox | — | Multi-row; header checkbox selects the filtered set only. |
| Status | wfx-badge pill | Set filter | See Section 4. F-1: pill severities differ from the panel badge — unify. |
| Doc No | Combined — Doc No (link, opens the panel) over “PO: {PONo} · GRN: {GRNNo}” | Text | Link via data-action="open-doc"; autoHeight on. |
| Doc Type | Document type | Set filter | — |
| Supplier | Combined — Supplier name over supplier code | Set filter | autoHeight on. |
| Doc Date | Combined — Doc Date over “Due: {DueDate}” | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | App-wide date format via WfxDateFormatService. Filters on the primary Doc Date only; the secondary Due date is not filterable from this cell (D-13). |
| GL Date | GL / accounting date | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | App-wide date format via WfxDateFormatService. |
| Doc Amount | Signed amount (Credit Notes negative) | Number | Right-aligned; symbol + 2 decimals + ISO code (e.g. “$45,200.00 USD”, “-$3,400.00 USD”). |
| Expected Pay Date | Expected payment date (Posted/both views only) | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | “—” when unset. |
| Created By | Creator — avatar chip + name | Set filter | WfxUserGroupCellRendererComponent; autoHeight on; blank renders “—”. |
| Created On | Creation date + time | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | App-wide date+time format. Filtering by a day matches any time on that day. |
• Default column config: resizable, sortable, floating filter on, min width 90.
• Row model: the mock grid is client-side (all rows loaded, filtered in the browser). The real screen must use the server-side row model with server paging/sort/filter (D-2).

#### Expected Pay From / To range filter
• Two separate date fields (From, To) plus a Clear button (shown once either is set), visible only when Posted documents can appear (Posted or cleared view). They let the clerk club everything due in a window before selecting.
• The range is inclusive on Expected Pay Date; the pickers cross-constrain (From’s maxDate = To, To’s minDate = From) so From ≤ To always holds (V-9). Documents without an expected date are excluded while a range is set.

#### Post & UnValidate (Validated selection)
• Post (primary): confirmation M-2, then each selected document moves Validated → Posted; the GL date already on the document is kept. Success M-3, selection cleared, list reloaded. Writes are strictly sequential (D-2).
• UnValidate (secondary): confirmation M-5, then each moves Validated → Draft and leaves this screen. Success M-6. Note F-3: no screen in this feature lists Draft documents, so an unvalidated document currently has no re-validation path — Q-2.

#### Assign Expected Payment Date (Posted selection)
• Modal “Assign Expected Payment Date”; helper “Set the expected payment date for {n} selected document(s). Must be today or later.” One required date picker (floor = today, V-5); Assign / Cancel.
• Assign with no date → warning M-8. On success the date is written to every selected document (sequential); success M-9. If the date is after any document’s Due Date, an additional warning M-10 names those documents but the assignment still proceeds (ASSUMED — Q-3).
• Assigning a date does not change status; the document stays Posted and now qualifies for the Payment Batch action (T-3).

#### Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)
Create Payment Batch — the Credit Note nets the total down ($33,000 − $1,200 = $31,800)
• The Payment Batch button appears only for an all-Posted selection where every document already carries an expected date (V-4). Opening the dialog is blocked if the selection spans more than one currency — warning M-12 (single-currency rule, V-7, Q-5).
• Dialog “Create Payment Batch”: a read-only summary (Documents count, Currency, Batch Total), a required Actual Payment Date picker, and a required Payment Mode select (Bank Transfer / Cheque / Cash / RTGS/Wire / LC / Online). Create Batch / Cancel.
• Batch Total is the net signed sum of the selected documents, so Credit Notes reduce it (V-10).
• Submit validates the date (M-13) and mode (M-14). On success a new batch is created in Draft with a snapshot of its member documents, and each member document moves Posted → In Batch (stamped with the batch no, actual date, and mode). Success M-15. The batch is released on S-2.
• Batch number is PB-{yyyy}-{seq}; in the mock seq is computed client-side (max existing id + 1), which the real server must own (D-4, F-6, Q-6).

### Payment Batches (S-2)
Purpose: the register of every payment batch, with drill-in to the member documents and the Confirm Payment / Cancel actions on Draft batches.
Payment Batches — one Paid and one Draft batch
Batch detail panel (Draft) — header, member-docs grid, and the Cancel Batch / Confirm Payment footer

#### Layout & grid

[TABLE 5: Table 5 · 9 rows · columns: Column (text), Content (text), Filter (text), Format / behaviour (text) · identifiers: Column]
| Column | Content | Filter | Format / behaviour |
| Status | wfx-badge pill | Set filter | Draft / Paid / Cancelled (Section 4). |
| Batch No | Combined — Batch No (link, opens the drawer) over Created On | Text | Link via data-action="open-batch". |
| Payment Date | Actual payment date | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | App-wide date format. |
| Payment Mode | Mode | Set filter | — |
| Currency | ISO code | Set filter | — |
| Total Amount | Net paid amount | Number | Right-aligned; symbol + 2 dp + code. |
| Docs | Member-document count | Number | Right-aligned. |
| Created By | Creator — avatar chip + name | Set filter | WfxUserGroupCellRendererComponent; autoHeight on; blank renders “—”. |
| Created On | Creation date + time | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | App-wide date+time format. |
• Quick search matches Batch No OR Payment Mode; a Status dropdown filters Draft / Paid / Cancelled. No row selection (actions are per-batch).
• Row context menu: Open (always); on a Draft batch also Confirm Payment and Cancel Batch (the same two actions as the drawer footer).

#### Batch detail panel & actions
• The drawer shows the batch header (Batch No, Status, Payment Date, Payment Mode, Currency, Total Amount, Documents, Created By, Created On) and a read-only “Documents in this Batch” grid built from the stored line snapshot.
• Footer actions appear only when the batch is Draft (V-11): Cancel Batch (danger) and Confirm Payment (primary).
• Confirm Payment: confirmation M-18, then the batch and every member document move to Paid (T-5/T-8). Success M-19. In the mock this only flips statuses — the real build must also execute the payment and post the payment GL entry (D-6, Q-8).
• Cancel Batch: confirmation M-21, then the batch moves to Cancelled and each member document reverts to Posted with its batch fields cleared; the expected payment date is retained so the document can be re-batched (T-6/T-9). Success M-22.
• Paid and Cancelled batches are terminal — no actions.

### Shared AP document detail panel (S-3)
Purpose: a read-only right drawer, opened from S-1, showing one document’s header and its balanced debit/credit journal preview. All state changes live on the parent list — the panel never mutates.
AP document detail panel — a posted Supplier Invoice; header, Dates & Payment (incl. Expected Payment), and the balanced Dr/Cr journal
• Header info: Doc No, Doc Type, Supplier “Name (Code)”, Status (badge), Doc Amount, PO No, GRN No.
• Dates & Payment: Doc Date, GL Date, Due Date, and — only when populated — Expected Payment, Payment Batch, Actual Payment, Payment Mode, then Created By, Created On.
• Accounting Entries (Dr / Cr): a grid of journal lines (Account name + code, Debit, Credit; zero amounts blank) with a pinned bottom Total row, then a status line: “Balanced — total debit equals total credit.” (success) or “Not balanced — please review the entries.” (error). The mock data is always balanced (V-12).
• The panel re-fetches when the document id (or a refreshKey) changes. Note F-5: the parent never bumps refreshKey, so a panel left open across an action can show stale header/status until re-opened.

### Alerts & messages (exact wording)

[TABLE 6: Table 6 · 23 rows · columns: # (text), Screen (text), Trigger (text), Kind (text), Title (text), Message (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Screen | Trigger | Kind | Title | Message |
| M-1 | AP Posting & Payments | AP documents failed to load | Error toast | Load Failed | Could not load AP documents from the mock store. |
| M-2 | AP Posting & Payments | Post confirmation | Confirm dialog | Post Documents | Post {n} validated document(s)? They move to the payment workflow (GL date unchanged). |
| M-3 | AP Posting & Payments | Post succeeded | Success toast | Documents Posted | {n} document(s) posted. |
| M-4 | AP Posting & Payments | Post failed | Error toast | Post Failed | Could not post one or more documents. |
| M-5 | AP Posting & Payments | UnValidate confirmation | Confirm dialog | UnValidate Documents | UnValidate {n} document(s)? They return to Draft and leave this screen until re-validated. |
| M-6 | AP Posting & Payments | UnValidate succeeded | Success toast | Documents UnValidated | {n} document(s) returned to Draft. |
| M-7 | AP Posting & Payments | UnValidate failed | Error toast | UnValidate Failed | Could not unvalidate one or more documents. |
| M-8 | AP Posting & Payments | Assign with no date | Warning toast | Validation | Please choose an expected payment date. |
| M-9 | AP Posting & Payments | Assign succeeded | Success toast | Expected Date Assigned | Expected payment date set on {n} document(s). |
| M-10 | AP Posting & Payments | Assigned date after due date | Warning toast | After Due Date | {n} document(s) have an expected date after their due date ({DocNos}). |
| M-11 | AP Posting & Payments | Assign failed | Error toast | Assign Failed | Could not assign the expected payment date. |
| M-12 | AP Posting & Payments | Selection spans multiple currencies | Warning toast | Mixed Currencies | A payment batch must be a single currency. Deselect documents so only one currency remains. |
| M-13 | AP Posting & Payments | Create with no actual date | Warning toast | Validation | Please choose an actual payment date. |
| M-14 | AP Posting & Payments | Create with no payment mode | Warning toast | Validation | Please choose a payment mode. |
| M-15 | AP Posting & Payments | Batch created | Success toast | Payment Batch Created | {batchNo} created as Draft with {n} document(s). Release it on the Payment Batches screen. |
| M-16 | AP Posting & Payments | Batch create failed | Error toast | Create Failed | Could not create the payment batch. |
| M-17 | Payment Batches | Payment batches failed to load | Error toast | Load Failed | Could not load payment batches from the mock store. |
| M-18 | Payment Batches | Confirm Payment confirmation | Confirm dialog | Confirm Payment | Confirm payment for {batchNo}? Its {docCount} document(s) will be marked Paid. |
| M-19 | Payment Batches | Payment confirmed | Success toast | Payment Confirmed | {batchNo} is now Paid. |
| M-20 | Payment Batches | Confirm failed | Error toast | Confirm Failed | Could not confirm the payment batch. |
| M-21 | Payment Batches | Cancel Batch confirmation | Confirm dialog | Cancel Batch | Cancel {batchNo}? Its document(s) return to Posted and can be re-batched. |
| M-22 | Payment Batches | Batch cancelled | Success toast | Batch Cancelled | {batchNo} was cancelled; its document(s) returned to Posted. |
| M-23 | Payment Batches | Cancel failed | Error toast | Cancel Failed | Could not cancel the payment batch. |
Confirmation dialogs are used for every state-changing action (Post, UnValidate, Confirm Payment, Cancel Batch) and spell out the impact; the real build must additionally gate these actions by role (D-7, Q-7).

## Workflow & status lifecycle

### AP document status

[TABLE 7: Table 7 · 5 rows · columns: Status (text), Meaning (text), Appears on (text) · identifiers: Status]
| Status | Meaning | Appears on |
| Draft | Captured but not validated. Upstream — set outside this feature. | Neither screen (F-3, Q-2) |
| Validated | Ready to post to the ledger. | AP Posting & Payments — To Post view |
| Posted | Posted to the ledger; being scheduled / batched. | AP Posting & Payments — Posted view |
| In Batch | Included in a Draft payment batch, awaiting release. | Read-only via its batch (S-2) |
| Paid | Batch confirmed; document settled. Terminal. | Read-only via its batch (S-2) |

### Payment batch status

[TABLE 8: Table 8 · 3 rows · columns: Status (text), Meaning (text)]
| Status | Meaning |
| Draft | Created; member documents are In Batch; can be Confirmed or Cancelled. |
| Paid | Confirmed; member documents are Paid. Terminal. |
| Cancelled | Cancelled; member documents reverted to Posted. Terminal. |

### Allowed transitions

[TABLE 9: Table 9 · 9 rows · columns: # (text), Transition (text), Trigger (text), Who / where (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Transition | Trigger | Who / where |
| T-1 | Validated → Posted | Post + confirmation (M-2); GL date unchanged | AP Posting & Payments (Validated selection) |
| T-2 | Validated → Draft | UnValidate + confirmation (M-5) | AP Posting & Payments (Validated selection) |
| T-3 | Posted → Posted (expected date set/revised) | Assign Expected Payment Date | AP Posting & Payments (Posted selection) |
| T-4 | Posted → In Batch | Included when a Draft batch is created | AP Posting & Payments (Payment Batch action) |
| T-5 | In Batch → Paid | Confirm Payment on the batch (M-18) | Payment Batches (S-2) |
| T-6 | In Batch → Posted | Cancel Batch (M-21); batch fields cleared, expected date kept | Payment Batches (S-2) |
| T-7 | (new) → Draft (batch) | Create Payment Batch | AP Posting & Payments (Payment Batch action) |
| T-8 | Draft → Paid (batch) | Confirm Payment (M-18) | Payment Batches (S-2) |
| T-9 | Draft → Cancelled (batch) | Cancel Batch (M-21) | Payment Batches (S-2) |
• Paid (document and batch) and Cancelled (batch) are terminal — no reopen. In the real build, undoing a confirmed payment is a reversal, not a status flip (D-6).
• Draft → Validated (the entry point of the To Post view) happens upstream and is out of scope; the UnValidate path (T-2) currently has no return route inside this feature (F-3, Q-2).
• Every transition above is behind a confirmation dialog that states the impact.

## Validations master list
One line per rule — related checks combined; shared display/enforcement rules are defined once under Conventions. Every rule is testable as written; inline messages show at the field, toasts per Section 3.

[TABLE 10: Table 10 · 13 rows · columns: # (text), Rule (testable statement) (text), Where enforced (text), Message (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Rule (testable statement) | Where enforced | Message |
| V-1 | Toolbar actions are selection-driven: Post/UnValidate for an all-Validated selection; Expected Pay Date for an all-Posted selection; Payment Batch additionally when every selected Posted doc has an expected date. Buttons are hidden when the selection doesn’t qualify (mixed or empty → none). | AP Posting & Payments | — |
| V-2 | AP Posting & Payments lists only Validated and Posted documents; the Status filter selects the stage (Validated by default, clear = both). | S-1 + server | — |
| V-3 | The Expected Pay Date column shows whenever Posted docs can appear (Posted or both view); hidden in the Validated-only view. | S-1 | — |
| V-4 | Payment Batch is offered only for an all-Posted selection where every document already has an Expected Payment Date. | S-1 + server | — |
| V-5 | Assign Expected Date requires a chosen date that is today or later (picker floor = today). | S-1 dialog | Please choose an expected payment date. |
| V-6 | If the assigned expected date is after a document’s Due Date, warn (naming the documents) but still proceed (ASSUMED — Q-3). | S-1 | {n} document(s) have an expected date after their due date ({DocNos}). |
| V-7 | A payment batch must be a single currency; a multi-currency selection cannot open the create dialog. | S-1 + server | A payment batch must be a single currency. Deselect documents so only one currency remains. |
| V-8 | Creating a batch requires an Actual Payment Date and a Payment Mode. | S-1 dialog | Please choose an actual payment date / a payment mode. |
| V-9 | Expected Pay From ≤ Expected Pay To (pickers cross-constrain); the range filter is inclusive on both ends and applies only in the Posted/both view. | S-1 toolbar | — |
| V-10 | A batch’s Total Amount is the net signed sum of its member documents (Credit Notes reduce it). | S-1 + server | — |
| V-11 | Confirm Payment and Cancel Batch are available only for Draft batches (footer + context menu); Paid/Cancelled are terminal. | S-2 + server | — |
| V-12 | Every document’s journal balances: ΣDebit = ΣCredit (the panel shows Balanced / Not balanced). | Posting engine (server) | Balanced — total debit equals total credit. / Not balanced — please review the entries. |
| V-13 | Batch number format is PB-{yyyy}-{4-digit sequence}; the sequence is server-assigned in the real build (D-4). | S-1 (mock) / server | — |

## Out-of-scope & deltas

### Mock shortcuts — full real behaviour required
The mock simplified reality in the following places. The real build must implement the FULL behaviour in the right-hand column; none of these shortcuts may silently become the product.

[TABLE 11: Table 11 · 13 rows · columns: # (text), Mock shortcut (text), Required real behaviour (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Mock shortcut | Required real behaviour |
| D-1 | The Dr/Cr journal is committed seed data in ap-document-gl-lines, shown as a static preview. | A GL posting engine derives the journal from the document (per doc-type posting rules), enforces balancing server-side, and posts it to the ledger on Post. The panel shows the actual posted journal. |
| D-2 | Client-side grid; bulk actions loop client-side, writing one record per request (sequential) to avoid the mock server dropping records. | Server-side row model (paging/sort/filter/search on the API); each bulk action is one atomic transactional request. Set-filter values from DDL APIs. |
| D-3 | Post only flips Status Validated → Posted. | Posting also writes the GL entries against GLDate, updates the supplier open-item/ledger, respects period-close (a closed period blocks posting), and is reversible only by a reversal — never a silent status flip. |
| D-4 | Batch number and BatchID are generated client-side (max existing id + 1), from a snapshot loaded at screen init. | Server-assigned sequence at create; the client never invents batch numbers. Prevents duplicate numbers under concurrency (F-6). |
| D-5 | Batch CreatedBy is hardcoded “Product Team”. | Set from the authenticated user; audited (D-8). |
| D-6 | Confirm Payment only flips the batch and its documents to Paid. | Executes the payment (bank file / cheque / RTGS per mode), posts the payment GL entry (Dr Accounts Payable, Cr Bank), records the payment reference, and enables reconciliation. Undo is a reversal, not a status flip. |
| D-7 | No permissions — every user sees every action. | Role-based permissions: clerks post and build batches; managers confirm/cancel payments (ASSUMED — Q-7). Unauthorized actions hidden or disabled. |
| D-8 | No audit trail on any action. | Post, UnValidate, Assign date, Create batch, Confirm, Cancel each logged with user + timestamp per ERP audit standards. |
| D-9 | A batch is single-currency; there is no FX handling. | Confirm single-currency-per-batch as the rule (Q-5); if multi-currency is ever needed, define the FX rate source and revaluation at payment. |
| D-10 | Expected payment date is a manual per-selection assignment with no scheduling logic. | May derive a suggested date from supplier payment terms and check cash availability before committing a batch (Q-3). |
| D-11 | The studio data-source fly-out (Team Data / Practice Copy / Start Empty) floats over every screen. | Studio-only tooling — must NOT be promoted into wfx-erp. |
| D-12 | Advances flow through the same post → schedule → batch pipeline as invoices. | Confirm with Finance how Advances behave in AP (typically paid on raising, then adjusted against future invoices) rather than assuming the invoice pipeline (Q-9). |
| D-13 | The combined Doc Date cell shows “Due: {DueDate}” as its secondary line, but a date filter compares one field, so Due Date cannot be filtered or sorted from that cell. | If AP needs to work by due date (an ageing / overdue view almost certainly does), give Due Date its own column with its own date filter rather than leaving it display-only. |

### Findings — mock defects and standards violations (do NOT implement)
Per the studio rule, standard violations found in the mock are flagged here instead of being specified; the spec body above states the corrected behaviour.

[TABLE 12: Table 12 · 6 rows · columns: # (text), Type (text), Screen / area (text), Finding (verified in code) (text), Corrected rule in this spec (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Type | Screen / area | Finding (verified in code) | Corrected rule in this spec |
| F-1 | Inconsistency | Status badge (grid vs panel) | The grid pill and the panel badge use different severity maps: Posted is green (success) in the grid but blue (info) in the panel, and Posted & Paid both render green in the grid — two distinct lifecycle states share a colour. | One status→severity map used everywhere, with a distinct severity per status (Section 4, 3.1). |
| F-2 | Bug — FIXED in the mock | Date columns (Doc Date, GL Date, Expected Pay Date, Created On, batch Payment Date) | These columns kept the default text filter while displaying formatted dates, so the floating filter matched the raw ISO string and filtering by what the user sees failed. Every date column now declares cellDataType: 'dateString' / 'dateTimeString' + filter: 'agDateColumnFilter', and wfx-grid supplies the parsing, inclusive ranges and calendar-day comparison generically. | Date columns use the date column filter — equals / before / after / from–to on a calendar picker (3.1.4, 3.2.1). Build the real screen this way; do not re-introduce a text filter on a date. |
| F-3 | Gap | UnValidate flow | UnValidate sends a document to Draft, but no screen in the feature lists Draft documents — it disappears with no re-validation path, though the confirm text promises “until re-validated”. | Provide a Draft/register screen or a re-validate action so unvalidated documents are recoverable (Q-2). |
| F-4 | Security | Grid cell renderers (both screens) | Renderers inject SupplierName, DocNo, CreatedBy and GL account names into innerHTML without escaping (only the status pill escapes). | Escape all interpolated text in cell renderers (or use component renderers). |
| F-5 | Bug | Shared doc panel | The parent passes only [apDocId] and never bumps the panel’s refreshKey, so a panel left open across an action can show stale header/status. | Bump refreshKey (or re-open) after each mutation (3.3). |
| F-6 | Bug | Payment Batch numbering | Next batch number derives from a client-side snapshot (max BatchID + 1); concurrent creates can mint duplicate PB numbers. | Server-assigned sequence at create (D-4, 3.1.8). |

## Open questions
The product team was not available for the pre-finalization batch, so every question carries a proposed default, which this spec ADOPTS AS ASSUMED and marks where used. Owner for every item: Product team / Finance (Varun Kumar) — confirmation required before development sign-off; any changed answer amends the referenced sections.

[TABLE 13: Table 13 · 14 rows · columns: # (text), Question (text), Adopted default (ASSUMED) (text), Used in (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Question | Adopted default (ASSUMED) | Used in |
| Q-1 | Does Post immediately post the journal to the ledger and respect period-close? | Yes — Post writes the GL entries against GLDate; a closed period blocks posting; reversible only by reversal. | D-1, D-3, 3.1.6 |
| Q-2 | After UnValidate, where do Draft documents live and how are they re-validated? | A Draft/AP register screen lists them with a re-validate action; UnValidate is allowed only before posting. | F-3, T-2 |
| Q-3 | Should an expected date after the due date be blocked or only warned? | Warn but allow (as mocked); flag overdue in reporting; a suggested date may come from supplier terms. | V-6, D-10 |
| Q-4 | Can the expected payment date be earlier than today (backdating)? | No — today or later (as mocked). | V-5 |
| Q-5 | Is a payment batch strictly single-currency? | Yes — one currency per batch; multiple currencies are separate batches. | V-7, D-9 |
| Q-6 | How is the batch number generated? | Server sequence “PB-{yyyy}-{seq}” at create; never client-side. | V-13, D-4, F-6 |
| Q-7 | Who may Post / UnValidate / Assign date / Create batch / Confirm / Cancel (roles)? | Clerks post & build batches; managers confirm/cancel payments; delete/cancel restricted to managers. | D-7 |
| Q-8 | Does Confirm Payment produce a real payment instrument and payment GL entry? | Yes — generates the bank file/cheque/RTGS, posts Dr AP / Cr Bank, records the payment reference, enables reconciliation. | D-6, 3.2.2 |
| Q-9 | How are Advances handled in AP — posted-then-batched like invoices, or paid at creation? | Confirm with Finance; this spec treats them in-pipeline as mocked pending that answer. | D-12 |
| Q-10 | May a Credit-Note-only batch (negative total) be created? | No — a Credit Note nets against invoices within a batch; a negative batch total is disallowed. | V-10 |
| Q-11 | Server paging, default sort, and list-state retention? | Server-side row model day one; page sizes 20/50/100 (default 20); Posted view sorted by Expected Pay Date asc; list state (filters, range, sort, page) restored on return. | D-2, Section 2 |
| Q-12 | How are the Dr/Cr accounts determined per document type? | From the AP posting rules per doc type/config (GRN clearing, input GST, AP trade, advance, freight, bank); owned by the posting engine, out of scope for these screens. | D-1 |
| Q-13 | Quick-search scope and debounce? | Doc No + Supplier name (batch list: Batch No + Payment Mode); 300 ms debounce. | 3.1.2 |
| Q-14 | Empty-state and load-error UX? | Per-view no-rows overlay (“No documents to post”, etc.) plus the load-error toasts as mocked (M-1, M-17). | 3.4 |

## Technical appendix — Data & API contract provisional
The committed mock JSON is the draft API contract; field names are PascalCase DTO names matching the intended real AP API. Three collections back the feature: ap-documents, ap-document-gl-lines, and payment-batches. The real backend must be reconciled field-by-field against these tables during promotion.

### GL journal line (ap-document-gl-lines)

[TABLE 15: Table 15 · 9 rows · columns: Field (text), Type (text), Example (text), Notes (text) · identifiers: Field]
| Field | Type | Example | Notes |
| id | string | gl-0101-1 | Mock record id. |
| APDocID | number (FK → ap-documents.APDocID) | 101 | Panel filters lines by this and sorts by LineNo. |
| LineNo | number | 1 | Line ordering. |
| GLAccountCode | string | 2010 | e.g. 5010 GRN Clearing, 1450 Input GST Receivable, 2010 Accounts Payable — Trade, 1610 Advance to Suppliers, 6300 Freight & Forwarding, 1010 Bank — Current. |
| GLAccountName | string | Accounts Payable — Trade | Shown with the code in the Account cell. |
| Debit | number | 0 | Right-aligned; blank when 0. |
| Credit | number | 45200 | Right-aligned; blank when 0. |
| CurrencyCode | string | USD | Matches the document currency. |
| Narration | string | Payable to Nishat Mills Ltd | Line description. |
Per document, exactly one of Debit / Credit is non-zero per line, and ΣDebit = ΣCredit (V-12). In the real build these lines are the OUTPUT of the posting engine, not stored seed data (D-1).

### Service surface

[TABLE 17: Table 17 · 6 rows · columns: Method (mock today) (text), Real endpoint (to define) (text), Notes (text) · identifiers: Method (mock today)]
| Method (mock today) | Real endpoint (to define) | Notes |
| fetchDocuments() | GET /ap-documents (server paging/sort/filter) | One call per grid block; no N+1. |
| getDocument(id) | GET /ap-documents/{id} | Panel header. |
| fetchGlLines(apDocId) | GET /ap-documents/{id}/gl-lines | Panel journal; server returns the posted journal. |
| saveDocument(doc) | POST /ap-documents/{id}/post, /unvalidate, /expected-date | Mock PUTs the whole record; real build exposes intent-specific endpoints that re-validate server-side. |
| fetchBatches() / getBatch(id) | GET /payment-batches[/{id}] | List + drawer. |
| saveBatch(batch) | POST /payment-batches, /{id}/confirm, /{id}/cancel | Server owns the batch-number sequence and the payment execution (D-4, D-6). |
• All reads/writes go through one thin per-feature service; components never call HTTP directly. On promotion the mock service is swapped for the real API-backed one and the screens are unchanged.
• Sequential writes: bulk actions (Post, UnValidate, Assign date, batch create, Confirm, Cancel) write one record at a time (RxJS concatMap). The mock server does read-modify-write per request, so parallel writes to one collection file drop records; the real transactional API should perform each bulk action as a single atomic request (D-2).
• The server is the source of truth for every rule in Section 6 — client validation is a convenience, not the enforcement.

CANDIDATES FOR REVIEW (possible definitions, formulas, validations, steps; not confirmed knowledge)
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments): The mock is intentionally lenient; this specification is not — it is the contract the development team builds from before it goes to QA and live production.
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Overview › Purpose): Accounts Payable (AP) takes a supplier-side document from “validated” through to “paid”.
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Overview › Purpose): A single status-aware screen, AP Posting & Payments, lets the AP clerk post validated documents to the ledger, schedule their expected payment dates, and gather dated documents into payment batches — without leaving the screen.
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Overview › Who uses it): AP clerks / accountants — post validated documents, assign expected payment dates, and assemble payment batches (all on one screen).
- workflow_steps (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Overview › Who uses it): Who uses it: / 1. AP clerks / accountants — post validated documents, assign expected payment dates, and assemble payment batches (all on one screen). / 2. AP / finance managers — confirm (release) or cancel payment batches. / 3. Downstream / reporting — read the resulting ledger entries and payment status; they do not act on these screens.
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Overview › Where it sits in the ERP?): In the Product Mock Studio it is mounted at /accounts-payable under the app base href /wfx-erp-product/, menu label “Accounts Payable” (icon pi pi-wallet).
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Overview › Where it sits in the ERP?): It is downstream of purchasing/GRN (which produce the documents) and upstream of the cash/bank and general-ledger modules (which the postings and payments feed).
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Overview › Where it sits in the ERP?): Document capture/validation (Draft → Validated) and the GL posting engine itself are upstream/downstream and out of scope (Section 7).
- table (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen inventory & navigation flow, table 1): Table 1: #, Screen, Route, Purpose (3 rows)

- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): There is no forced wizard — the clerk works the stage they need via the Status filter on S-1.
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Drawers are dismissible (X / overlay / hide); they never navigate away from the list.
- workflow_steps (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Navigation rules: / 1. The two screens are sibling menu links under Accounts Payable. There is no forced wizard — the clerk works the stage they need via the Status filter on S-1. / 2. List → detail panel: on S-1, clicking the Doc No link (data-action="open-doc") opens the shared right drawer (S-3). On S-2, clicking the Batch No link (data-action="open-batch") opens the batch detail drawer. / 3. Drawers are dismissible (X / overlay / hide); they never navigate away from the list. / 4. Documents move between stages by status, not by routing: after any action the list reloads and the acted-on rows drop off if they no longer qualify for the current Status filter. / 5. Browser/page titles come from the route title: “AP Posting & Payments”, “Payment Batches”.

- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Status filter & views): The list is ordered with dated documents first (ascending by expected date, which helps batching), then undated documents.

The Status filter has two options — To Post (Validated) and Posted — and defaults to Validated. Clearing it shows both stages at once. / 2. The Expected Pay Date column shows whenever Posted documents can appear (Posted view or the cleared “both” view); it is hidden in the Validated-only view. / 3. Switching the Status filter clears the current selection so the action buttons stay honest. Only Validated and Posted documents ever appear on this screen (Draft/In Batch/Paid do not). / 4. The list is ordered with dated documents first (ascending by expected date, which helps batching), then undated documents.

- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Post & UnValidate (Validated selection)): Post (primary): confirmation M-2, then each selected document moves Validated → Posted; the GL date already on the document is kept.

- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Assign Expected Payment Date (Posted selection)): If the date is after any document’s Due Date, an additional warning M-10 names those documents but the assignment still proceeds (ASSUMED — Q-3).
- workflow_steps (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Assign Expected Payment Date (Posted selection)): Assign Expected Payment Date (Posted selection): / 1. Modal “Assign Expected Payment Date”; helper “Set the expected payment date for {n} selected document(s). Must be today or later.” One required date picker (floor = today, V-5); Assign / Cancel. / 2. Assign with no date → warning M-8. On success the date is written to every selected document (sequential); success M-9. If the date is after any document’s Due Date, an additional warning M-10 names those documents but the assignment still proceeds (ASSUMED — Q-3). / 3. Assigning a date does not change status; the document stays Posted and now qualifies for the Payment Batch action (T-3).
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): Opening the dialog is blocked if the selection spans more than one currency — warning M-12 (single-currency rule, V-7, Q-5).
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): Opening the dialog is blocked if the selection spans more than one currency — warning M-12 (single-currency rule, V-7, Q-5).
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): Batch Total is the net signed sum of the selected documents, so Credit Notes reduce it (V-10).
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): Submit validates the date (M-13) and mode (M-14).
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): On success a new batch is created in Draft with a snapshot of its member documents, and each member document moves Posted → In Batch (stamped with the batch no, actual date, and mode).
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): The batch is released on S-2.
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): Batch number is PB-{yyyy}-{seq}; in the mock seq is computed client-side (max existing id + 1), which the real server must own (D-4, F-6, Q-6).
- formula (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): Batch number is PB-{yyyy}-{seq}; in the mock seq is computed client-side (max existing id + 1), which the real server must own (D-4, F-6, Q-6).
- workflow_steps (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › AP Posting & Payments (S-1) › Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection)): Create Payment Batch (dated Posted selection): / 1. The Payment Batch button appears only for an all-Posted selection where every document already carries an expected date (V-4). Opening the dialog is blocked if the selection spans more than one currency — warning M-12 (single-currency rule, V-7, Q-5). / 2. Dialog “Create Payment Batch”: a read-only summary (Documents count, Currency, Batch Total), a required Actual Payment Date picker, and a required Payment Mode select (Bank Transfer / Cheque / Cash / RTGS/Wire / LC / Online). Create Batch / Cancel. / 3. Batch Total is the net signed sum of the selected documents, so Credit Notes reduce it (V-10). / 4. Submit validates the date (M-13) and mode (M-14). On success a new batch is created in Draft with a snapshot of its member documents, and each member document moves Posted → In Batch (stamped with the batch no, actual date, and mode). Success M-15. The batch is released on S-2. / 5. Batch number is PB-{yyyy}-{seq}; in the mock seq is computed client-side (max existing id + 1), which the real server must own (D-4, F-6, Q-6).
- table (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › Payment Batches (S-2) › Layout & grid, table 5): Table 5: Column, Content, Filter, Format / behaviour (9 rows; identifiers: Column)
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › Payment Batches (S-2) › Batch detail panel & actions): Footer actions appear only when the batch is Draft (V-11): Cancel Batch (danger) and Confirm Payment (primary).
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › Payment Batches (S-2) › Batch detail panel & actions): Footer actions appear only when the batch is Draft (V-11): Cancel Batch (danger) and Confirm Payment (primary).
- validation (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › Payment Batches (S-2) › Batch detail panel & actions): In the mock this only flips statuses — the real build must also execute the payment and post the payment GL entry (D-6, Q-8).
- definition (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › Payment Batches (S-2) › Batch detail panel & actions): Paid and Cancelled batches are terminal — no actions.
- workflow_steps (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › Payment Batches (S-2) › Batch detail panel & actions): Batch detail panel & actions: / 1. The drawer shows the batch header (Batch No, Status, Payment Date, Payment Mode, Currency, Total Amount, Documents, Created By, Created On) and a read-only “Documents in this Batch” grid built from the stored line snapshot. / 2. Footer actions appear only when the batch is Draft (V-11): Cancel Batch (danger) and Confirm Payment (primary). / 3. Confirm Payment: confirmation M-18, then the batch and every member document move to Paid (T-5/T-8). Success M-19. In the mock this only flips statuses — the real build must also execute the payment and post the payment GL entry (D-6, Q-8). / 4. Cancel Batch: confirmation M-21, then the batch moves to Cancelled and each member document reverts to Posted with its batch fields cleared; the expected payment date is retained so the document can be re-batched (T-6/T-9). - workflow_steps (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Screen specifications › Shared AP document detail panel (S-3)): Shared AP document detail panel (S-3): / 1. Header info: Doc No, Doc Type, Supplier “Name (Code)”, Status (badge), Doc Amount, PO No, GRN No. / 2. Dates & Payment: Doc Date, GL Date, Due Date, and — only when populated — Expected Payment, Payment Batch, Actual Payment, Payment Mode, then Created By, Created On. / 3. Accounting Entries (Dr / Cr): a grid of journal lines (Account name + code, Debit, Credit; zero amounts blank) with a pinned bottom Total row, then a status line: “Balanced — total debit equals total credit.” (success) or “Not balanced — please review the entries.” (error). The mock data is always balanced (V-12). / 4. The panel re-fetches when the document id (or a refreshKey) changes. Note F-5: the parent never bumps refreshKey, so a panel left open across an action can show stale header/status until re-opened.

- workflow_steps (§ Accounts Payable — Posting & Payments › Technical appendix — Data & API contract provisional › Service surface): Service surface: / 1. All reads/writes go through one thin per-feature service; components never call HTTP directly. On promotion the mock service is swapped for the real API-backed one and the screens are unchanged. / 2. Sequential writes: bulk actions (Post, UnValidate, Assign date, batch create, Confirm, Cancel) write one record at a time (RxJS concatMap). The mock server does read-modify-write per request, so parallel writes to one collection file drop records; the real transactional API should perform each bulk action as a single atomic request (D-2). / 3. The server is the source of truth for every rule in Section 6 — client validation is a convenience, not the enforcement.
